newsitem.title: UK: LPC-Israel mandates banks for $200 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: LPC-Israel mandates banks for $200 mln loan.

text.p: LONDON, Sept 17 (LPC) - The State of Israel has mandated five banks to arrange a $200 million syndicated loan, according to banking sources.
NatWest Markets, Bank Hapoalim, Banque Nationale de Paris, Bayerische Landesbank and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank were awarded the mandate.
The credit has a final maturity of seven years, bankers said.

This is substantially longer than the maturity on a $100 million credit Israel took in 1995. That loan was arranged by Bank Leumi, BZW and Chemical Bank and was split between a four-year element priced 45 bps over LIBOR and a five-year element with a margin of 50 bps.
Pricing for the new deal could not be learned, but bankers were confident Israel will achieve a rate well inside that of 1995.
In December 1995, Standard & Poor's raised Israel's long-term foreign currency debt rating to A minus, from BBB plus, citing the government's commitment to reducing its debt burden.
Israel also plans a $750 million note programme and a $200 million Eurobond in the fourth quarter, both to be led by Merrill Lynch.
